title: Interpreting Speckle Effects Through Neuron Interventions
abstract: arXiv:2611.33632v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Speckle, the multiplicative noise inherent to synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, reduces the performance of pretrained SAR models. We use interpretability methods to examine its effects inside pretrained vision models. We identify neurons that respond selectively to speckle and test whether correcting their activations improves reconstruction. We study SARMAE, an Earth observation model pretrained on a million-scale SAR dataset. Synthetic scenes with known reflectivity allow us to measure recovery precisely. The model contains 38 speckle-selective neurons that track speckle's value distribution. Restoring these neurons to their clean values does not improve reconstruction. Activation patching across layers shows that the first MLP has the largest restoration and injection effects. Within this layer, a different set of 64 neurons recovers 44.1\% of the correlation loss on held-out scenes. When the speckle-selective neurons are held

translated_title: 通过神经元干预解释斑点效应
translated_abstract: 斑点是合成孔径雷达（SAR）成像中固有的乘性噪声，会降低预训练SAR模型的性能。我们使用可解释性方法来考察其对预训练视觉模型内部的影响。我们识别出对斑点有选择性响应的神经元，并测试纠正这些神经元的激活是否能改善重建效果。我们研究了SARMAE——一个在百万规模SAR数据集上预训练的地球观测模型。具有已知反射率的合成场景使我们能够精确测量恢复效果。该模型包含38个追踪斑点值分布的斑点选择性神经元。然而，将这些神经元恢复到其干净值并不能改善重建。跨层的激活修补（activation patching）实验表明，第一个MLP层具有最大的恢复和注入效应。在该层内部，另一组共64个神经元在保留测试场景上恢复了44.1%的相关性损失。当斑点选择性神经元被保持……
tldr: 研究发现，SAR预训练模型中的斑点信息并非由斑点选择性神经元直接编码，而是主要由第一个MLP层的64个神经元承载，修复这些神经元可恢复44.1%的相关性损失。
en_tdlr: Through neuron interventions and activation patching, this study reveals that speckle information in a pretrained SAR model is not encoded by speckle-selective neurons but primarily by 64 neurons in the first MLP layer, whose repair recovers 44.1% of the correlation loss.
